chunk_findings.detail: `walked = self.help is not None and words[0] in self.help.commands` is evaluated before the length guard. Previously the first statement was `if len(words) < _VERB_WORDS ...`, which short-circuited safely on an empty token list. Now, if `_command` is ever called with an empty or whitespace-only string, `s.split()` returns `[]` and `words[0]` raises `IndexError` instead of returning `False`. The moved length check on the next line no longer protects that access, so any call site that can pass an empty snippet crashes the whole check run.

chunk_findings.detail: When a command appears in both `self.cmds` (the project's tracked scripts) and `self.help.commands` (configured via `[docs].cli_command`), the corpus branch wins and the walked help is never consulted for the verb check: the condition `if words[0] in self.cmds and verb not in self.corpus.verbs` fires before the `elif walked` branch. So if `help_commands` includes a project script (a reasonable configuration — e.g. `cli_command = ["ddflow"]` so that `ddflow <verb> --flag` mentions are validated against `--help`), and a doc references `ddflow newverb` where `newverb` is real per `ddflow --help` but not yet registered in the tracked-code corpus, the checker emits a false "command" finding (`no tracked code registers 'newverb' as a command`) instead of letting `--help` be the authority. The walked check should take precedence (or be consulted before flagging the verb as unregistered).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck.py:380

chunk_findings.detail: Tool names extracted from sources can contain spaces (the intent's whole point is `<tool> <verb>` mentions, e.g. `ddflow docs check`), but documentation text is tokenized only by `_WORD_TOKEN = [REDACTED] which splits on whitespace. So a document that says "use `ddflow docs check`" yields words {ddflow, docs, check, ...} but never the string `ddflow docs check`; `s.name in words` is therefore always False for any multi-word tool name, and `undocumented` emits a `command` finding claiming no document mentions it even though it does. The same applies to knobs whose extracted names contain characters outside the word pattern. This is a guaranteed false-positive for exactly the case the feature exists to check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck_extract.py:undocumented

chunk_findings.detail: `_FENCE` is `^\s*(`{3,}|~{3,})(.*)$`, which accepts any amount of leading whitespace. CommonMark only treats a fence as a fence when indented at most 3 spaces; with 4+ spaces the line is an indented code block whose content is literal text. Given a document containing a line `    ```python` (four leading spaces, e.g. an indented snippet of markdown source), GitHub renders the following lines as normal prose, but `lines()` opens a code region there, so `prose_only` blanks every subsequent line (and `anchors_of` skips every subsequent heading) until a matching "closing" fence appears — all flag/command/anchor claims in the rest of the document are silently missed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docscheck_md.py:lines / _FENCE
